llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions line up with a CLI-based image-generation client (npm package / npx usage); nothing requested is unrelated to that purpose, though there are small bookkeeping inconsistencies and expected privacy implications you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a thin CLI client for dLazy's Banana2 image generation and the SKILL.md, metadata, and required binaries (npm, npx) are consistent with installing/running an npm CLI (@dlazy/cli). The declared API endpoints and config path match the described SaaS flow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to run the dlazy CLI and state that local files passed as images will be uploaded to oss.dlazy.com and prompts/params will be sent to api.dlazy.com — this is coherent for a cloud image-generation client but means user files and prompts are transmitted to an external service. The SKILL.md also references using the DLAZY_API_KEY env var even though 'required env vars' is empty in the registry metadata (minor documentation mismatch).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec in the registry), but metadata suggests installing a pinned npm package (@dlazy/cli@1.0.8) or running via npx. Installing a CLI from npm is an expected mechanism here but carries standard risks of executing third-party code; prefer npx (ephemeral) or review the GitHub repo before global install. There is a slight version inconsistency: registry lists version 1.0.6, SKILL.md shows 1.0.3, while the install target is @dlazy/cli@1.0.8.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No unrelated credentials are requested. The dLazy API key is required by the service (stored in ~/.dlazy/config.json or passed via DLAZY_API_KEY) which is proportionate to the CLI's function. Note the skill will persist your API key in user config if you use 'dlazy auth set', so protect/rotate that key as needed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install-time forced persistence are set. The skill does not request elevated or cross-skill privileges and does not modify other skills' configs according to the provided files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward wrapper for the dLazy CLI, but take these precautions before installing or using it: 1) Review the @dlazy/cli GitHub repository and the exact npm package version (the SKILL.md references @dlazy/cli@1.0.8 while other version fields differ). 2) Prefer running with npx to avoid a global install. 3) Be aware that any local images or prompts you pass will be uploaded to dLazy's servers (oss.dlazy.com) — do not send sensitive content. 4) Keep your DLAZY_API_KEY secret, store it only if you accept that it will be saved to ~/.dlazy/config.json, and rotate/revoke the key if needed. 5) If you need higher assurance, inspect the CLI source code or run the CLI in a controlled environment and monitor network calls to confirm it only contacts the documented endpoints.
